pages.text: Amo loves playing in the mielie garden and listening to the birds sing.
pages.change: We meet Amo and the two things she loves: the mielies and the birds

notes: Amo from behind, a butterfly on her finger; a row of ripe cobs on the right; brown birds swoop over the field, one right at a cob
illustration.only_in_image: A bird is already diving at a cob on the first spread — the culprit is planted before the problem exists.

pages.label: OBSERVED

pages.text:
Every day after school, she goes to count the mielies.
“Mielies! Mielies!”
She calls out.
pages.action: calls out to the mielies before counting
pages.change: A daily ritual is set: after school she comes to count the mielies

notes: Round portrait of Amo, hands at her chest, sun and butterflies around her

pages.label: OBSERVED

pages.change: The count is fixed: six mielies

notes: Amo points at a row of six cobs under the sun; numerals across the top
illustration.only_in_image: Six cobs are drawn in a row so the listener can count along and check her.

pages.label: OBSERVED

pages.text:
“Come on, Amo! Let’s have lunch!”
Koko calls her.
pages.change: Grandmother Koko enters and the day's ritual ends with lunch

notes: Koko seen from behind, waving; Amo skips down a yellow path

pages.label: OBSERVED

pages.text:
“When can we eat the mielies, Koko?” Amo asks.
“Soon,” Koko always answers.
pages.action: Amo asks when they can eat the mielies
pages.change: Amo's wish to eat the mielies is stated; Koko's answer is always 'soon'
pages.question_created: When will the mielies be ready?

notes: Kitchen: Koko and Amo face each other; two bottles and a lemon on a shelf; two pale bottles drawn again on the facing page
illustration.only_in_image: Plastic-looking bottles sit on the shelf and on the facing page — the later solution is planted in the picture long before Koko names it.

pages.label: INFERRED

pages.text:
The next afternoon Amo goes to count the mielies.
1 … 2 … 3 … 4 … 5 …
Oh no!
pages.action: counts and comes up one short
pages.change: The count stops at five: something is wrong
pages.question_created: Where did the sixth mielie go?
pages.page_turn_note: The count breaks off before six; the 'Oh no!' sits on the right-hand page.

notes: Round garden picture: six stalks, one without a cob; a bird's tail at the top edge; corn kernels scattered across both pages
illustration.only_in_image: One stalk stands empty, a bird's tail pokes in at the top and kernels lie on the ground: the picture shows what happened while the text only says 'Oh no!'.

pages.label: OBSERVED

notes: Close-up of a hand, fingers numbered one to five; bird wings frame the corners; kernels and beetles
illustration.only_in_image: Bird wings enter the frame from both corners around her counting hand, and kernels are spilled near it.

pages.text:
“Koko!
One mielie is missing!”
“Let’s have lunch now, we’ll check the mielies tomorrow.”
pages.action: Amo reports the loss; Koko postpones
pages.change: The problem is spoken aloud; the adult defers it to tomorrow

notes: Amo, arms spread, in front of the field; Koko calmly holds a pink flower, looking away
illustration.only_in_image: Koko is calm and turned away holding a flower while Amo is alarmed — the picture shows the gap between their worries.

pages.label: INFERRED

pages.text:
Amo goes to the garden with Koko the next day.
“Mielies! Mielies!” she calls out.
1 … 2 … 3 … 4 …
She stops.
pages.change: The count breaks even earlier: the loss is growing
pages.page_turn_note: The spread ends with the count cut off and 'She stops.'; answered on the next spread.

notes: Tall cobs with feathers stuck to them and feathers drifting; on the right fewer cobs and empty stalks
illustration.only_in_image: Feathers cling to the cobs and drift in the air — the culprit's traces.

pages.label: OBSERVED

pages.text:
“Koko! Now two mielies are missing! What happened?”
“Hmm … I think the birds ate them,” says Koko.
Amo is sad.
“Do we have to chase them away?”
pages.action: Koko names the birds; Amo asks if they must chase them away
pages.change: The thief is the birds she loves; she faces a conflict between her two loves
pages.question_created: Must the birds be chased away?
pages.page_turn_note: Ends on Amo's question, answered by Koko's idea.

notes: A large bird perched on a cob, beak open; Amo points, Koko frowns beside her
illustration.only_in_image: The bird is shown on the cob, mid-theft, on the same spread where Koko only guesses.

pages.label: OBSERVED

pages.text:
“I have an idea!” says Koko.
“Let’s get some plastic bottles.”
pages.change: Koko has an idea that will need plastic bottles

notes: Mostly empty pale page; large cut-open green bottle shapes in the lower foreground
illustration.only_in_image: The bottles are drawn cut open, hinting at how they will be used.

pages.label: INFERRED

pages.text: “See! Now the mielies are safe, and you can still see the birds.”
pages.action: they watch the protected field and the birds
pages.change: The mielies are safe and the birds still fly: both loves are kept

notes: Sunset over hills; each cob wrapped in a clear bottle sleeve; birds fly above; Koko's arm around Amo
illustration.only_in_image: Only the picture shows how the idea works: each cob sits inside a cut plastic bottle. Koko's arm around Amo closes the scene.

pages.label: OBSERVED
